answer: New agents earn the right to transact by completing verifiable useful work: each identity must finish small tasks—data checks, code reviews—graded by randomly assigned peers before it can trade. A reputation signal accumulates only from verified work, so a sybil faces the full labor cost per fake identity; a gale of cheap clones earns nothing. Over a long horizon, trusted agents compound their standing while idle or fraudulent identities stay locked out, making mass forgery more expensive than honest participation.
